research_mode: official Home Office primary statistical guidance only; stop-and-search data-quality methodology gates; no parcel result, exact incident location or local-risk score claimed

sources.name: Stop-and-search accredited-statistics status
verified_claims: The core stop-and-search series is labelled Accredited Official Statistics after independent statistical review.
limitations: Accreditation does not remove the specific missing-data and comparability limitations documented in the bulletin.

sources.name: Stop-and-search force coverage
verified_claims: The series receives data from all 43 territorial police forces and British Transport Police.
limitations: Coverage does not mean every force supplied every requested breakdown or field.

sources.name: BTP time-series comparability
verified_claims: British Transport Police data has been included from the year ending March 2010, so earlier totals are not directly comparable.
limitations: The relatively small BTP share does not make pre-2010 and later series strictly identical.

sources.name: Incident-level stop-and-search collection
verified_claims: Since the year ending March 2021 forces have supplied stop-and-search data in incident-level format under the Annual Data Requirement.
limitations: Incident-level structure improves analysis but does not ensure each record is complete or correct.

sources.name: Duplicate-record quality check
verified_claims: Home Office quality reports flag potential duplicate stop-and-search records for force review.
limitations: A quality check does not prove all duplicates were detected or corrected.

sources.name: Unusual-age quality check
verified_claims: Home Office quality reports flag records containing unusual age values.
limitations: Flagging does not establish the correct age for an affected record.

sources.name: Date-and-time quality check
verified_claims: Incorrect or unusual date and time data is included in the Home Office quality-review process.
limitations: A published month must not be treated as exact incident timing without record-level evidence.

sources.name: Unusual-volume quality check
verified_claims: Unusual changes in force stop-and-search volumes are queried during quality assurance.
limitations: A large change may reflect operations, policy, recording or correction and is not automatically an error.

sources.name: Force revision process
verified_claims: Forces may submit revised stop-and-search datasets after reviewing quality issues.
limitations: Published figures are correct at publication time but may later be revised.

sources.name: Excluded-force comparison rule
verified_claims: Forces unable to supply requested breakdowns may be excluded from specified annual comparisons, with exclusions identified in table notes.
limitations: National totals and comparison subsets may therefore have different coverage.

sources.name: Missing self-defined ethnicity
verified_claims: Eighteen percent of stop-and-search records in the year ending March 2025 did not contain self-defined ethnicity.
limitations: Missingness may arise because ethnicity was not provided or was not requested, and is not a valid basis for assigning an ethnic category.

sources.name: Ethnicity disclosure is not compulsory
verified_claims: A person stopped and searched is not legally required under PACE guidance to provide ethnicity.
limitations: A missing value must not be treated as refusal, officer omission or any particular ethnicity without evidence.

sources.name: Officer-observed ethnicity fallback
verified_claims: Officer-observed ethnicity may be used where self-defined ethnicity is unavailable to support more complete analysis.
limitations: Observed categories are less detailed and do not include a distinct Mixed category, so the two measures are not equivalent.

sources.name: Unknown-age treatment
verified_claims: Age values recorded as zero are reported as unknown, and age was unknown for 4.5% of searches in the year ending March 2025.
limitations: Unknown age cannot be allocated to an age band for local profiling.

sources.name: Reason-for-arrest development status
verified_claims: Reason-for-arrest following stop and search is published as Official Statistics in development because some force systems default or overuse generic categories.
limitations: Alignment between search reason and arrest reason must not be assumed from these developing fields.

sources.name: Outcome-link quality boundary
verified_claims: Outcome-linked-to-search-reason statistics are not labelled Accredited Official Statistics because of known quality issues.
limitations: An outcome should not be treated as caused by or matched to a search reason without the validated linkage field.

sources.name: Person-ID repeat-search limitation
verified_claims: Voluntary person-ID data is intended to study repeated searches but is often missing or incorrectly reused across individuals.
limitations: Repeat-search counts must not be inferred from unreliable or missing person IDs.

sources.name: Force recording-system variation
verified_claims: Forces use different mobile and case-management systems, including shared and bespoke configurations, to record encounters.
limitations: Field availability and workflow can differ by force and system version.

sources.name: Stop-and-search location accuracy
verified_claims: Forces reported that manually entered locations or coordinates derived from addresses can make stop-and-search location data inexact.
limitations: A published coordinate must not be treated as an exact incident point or parcel match.

sources.name: Free-text consistency limitation
verified_claims: Free-text recording can vary between records and reduce consistency and reliability of analysis.
limitations: Free-text values require normalization and review before aggregation or classification.
